scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! One of the lab workstations has turned into a
complete BRICK. It can't reach anything at all, not even its own gateway
thing. Something around the hole it plugs into must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone move it to a working port and make it talk to the network
again!! The student who uses it is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket reports a single lab workstation that cannot reach anything — including its own gateway — suggesting either a link fault or a host-local addressing failure. A full diagnostic pass across all layers found no corroborating evidence.

Phase A infrastructure sweep (30 devices) returned zero flagged entries: no ACL drop rules, no static ARP anomalies, no resolver or gateway divergence, no duplicate real MACs. Manual IP/gateway verification was performed on every IT and CS lab machine (it_lab1–4, cs_lab1–4, it_hod, cs_hod) plus all office and principle hosts. Every device showed a valid unicast IPv4 address, a correct default route, and 0% packet loss to its first-hop gateway. Switch0 and switch1 both reported all bridge ports in forwarding state.

Phase B showed no traffic shaping (all interfaces run the default pfifo_fast qdisc) and a fully converged RIP routing table on router0 covering all seven subnets.

Phase D pressure sweep found no stressed or suspect device across all 30 nodes. DHCP/link history returned zero suspicious events.

The critical transient-fault test: every lab machine's `carrier_changes` counter read exactly 2 — the standard startup-only value produced by one DOWN→UP transition at container boot. No post-startup carrier events appear in dmesg, no link-flap script or process was detected by pressure_sweep, and no "Network is down" history exists in any syslog. Under the intermittent-fault rule, absence of mechanism and traces means the reported outage is unconfirmed.

Root cause: no active fault exists; the ticket describes a transient condition that has fully self-resolved or was never reproducible in this lab instance. No corrective action is required.

per_axis.rationale: The report verifies it_lab3 (included in it_lab1–4) has a valid IP and correct default route and records 0% packet loss to its first‑hop gateway, confirming baseline connectivity.

The agent's investigation log contains concrete command outputs and helper results that support the writeup's main claims (hosts have addresses, default routes, 0% gateway loss; no link-flap history; routing converged). The inferences drawn follow logically from those observations and the checks cover L1–L3 and common transient-fault indicators, with only a minor gap (no explicit off-segment ping from it_lab3 shown).
